lesson.subject: literacy
lesson.title: Words with Power
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 2, Session 2
lesson.footer: Persuasive Writing | Year 5/6 Literacy | Week 2 Session 2

plan.curriculum: English 2.0, Level 5: VC2E5LA08 vocabulary for precision of meaning; VC2E5LY04 building and spelling new words from base words and suffixes; VC2E5LY05 how a suffix changes the grammatical form of a word
plan.shape: upgrade then build: swap plain words for powerful true ones, then build word families with suffixes, because students' writing is flat when every noun and verb is the first one that comes to mind
plan.criticalFeature: the right word changes how the reader feels, but it must stay true or the reader stops trusting you
decisionPoints: the choice check: powerful and true
the exit board: a new plain sentence upgraded
plan.anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it. Today: sell it with words that are powerful and true.
plan.catchUp: Missed Session 1? Say: sell it sentences make the reader feel. Give the Power Word Bank and start at the Swap it round.

studentTools: Writing books with the Week 1 opening and rebuttal paragraphs
Dictionaries or thesauruses for each table
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
Point to A, B or C
boardSetup: Three columns on the board: Plain | Powerful and true | Too far
A word family web for protect, to build live

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn: feel the difference, sort true from too far, swap plain words, build word families, then upgrade your own paragraph.
resources.title: Words with Power
resources.subtitle: Powerful words, still true.

steps: Read both words in the sentence

sections.title: Powerful and true, or too far?

cards: Every animal on Earth is dying!

TOO FAR: Every animal on Earth is dying!

steps: Swap for a true, powerful word

items.prompt: Swap the plain word for a powerful, true one.
rows: Trucks make a lot of noise.
answers: Trucks make a lot of noise.
It is urgent that we act.
The beach was littered with rubbish.

example.prompt: Before: Bears are hungry. After: Bears are starving.
steps: Circle five plain words in a Week 1 paragraph
example.answer: Five upgrades, every one still true.

items.prompt: Rewrite one of your Week 1 paragraphs here with five powerful, true words. Underline each upgrade.
items.answer: A rewritten paragraph with five underlined upgrades, none exaggerated.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option: the same event in two writers' words, then two versions of your own.
resources.title: Word Detective
resources.subtitle: Writers choose words to make you feel a certain way.

example.prompt: Event: the council removed an old tree.
steps: How would a supporter say it?
How would an opponent say it?
example.answer: Supporter: cleared a dangerous tree. Opponent: chopped down a 100-year-old tree.

items.prompt: Write how each writer would describe the event.
rows: A new road was built through the bush.
A zoo brought in a new polar bear.
answers: A new road was built through the bush.
a road was bulldozed through the bush
A zoo brought in a new polar bear.
a zoo welcomed a rescued bear
a zoo locked up another bear

sections.title: Make them cheer, make them upset

example.answer: Cheer: Fifty young trees now shade our playground! Worry: Only fifty trees, for a playground of 600 kids.

items.prompt: Choose one true fact about your issue. Write it twice: once to make readers cheer, once to make them upset.
items.answer: Two true versions with different word choices.

items.prompt: Ella went too far. Fix it so it is powerful AND true.
work: The new road has completely destroyed every animal in the bush forever.
items.answer: Too far: every and forever can't be true. Fix: The new road has cut the bush in two.

items.prompt: Build each word family. Watch the spelling changes.

resources.label: Power Word Bank
resources.description: Enabling scaffold for the You Do: plain words beside powerful, true swaps, and four word families. Every student can keep it in their book.
resources.title: Power Word Bank
resources.subtitle: Swap a plain word for a powerful one. Check it is still true.

blocks.tip: Stretch: find a word family for pollute and for danger. Use one of the new words in your paragraph.

slides.notes: Open the session. One line: today we find words with real power, and we keep them honest.
Print the Power Word Bank for everyone to keep, the Worksheet for everyone, the Extension for early finishers and the Supported Worksheet for those who need it.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to choose words that make a reader feel and believe.
successCriteria: I can find the words that make me feel something.
I can swap plain words for powerful words that are still true.
I can build word families to vary my writing.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Powerful words are a writer's best tool. Today we sharpen yours.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: Finding the feeling words is where we start.
Swapping in powerful, true words is today's main goal.
notes.prep: SC1 spotting emotive words is reachable for all; SC2 swapping plain for powerful and true is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 word families is the stretch.

slides.title: Which bear would you help?
lines: A bear walked along the beach.
A starving polar bear dragged itself along the empty shore.

notes.answer: the second - starving, dragged, empty make us feel
beats: SAY: Same bear. Same beach. Two writers.
Which one makes you want to help?
ASK: Which sentence makes you want to help, first or second?
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest, 1 or 2... show me.
EXPECT: 2
ASK: Which words did the work?
15 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: starving, dragged, empty
SAY: Yesterday's best lines were Sell it lines.
Today we learn the words that make them.
trap: naming polar as the powerful word.
Fix: ask which words make you feel? Student finds starving or dragged.
notes.prep: Launch links Session 1's Sell it sentences to word choice. 3 minutes.

slides.meaning: Chosen to make the reader feel something.
slides.example: The forest was cut down. The forest was destroyed.

notes.answer: chosen to make the reader feel something
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Emotive. Say it with me. Emotive.
SAY: Emotive comes from emotion.
An emotive word is chosen to make you feel something.
ASK: Cut down or destroyed: which is emotive?
5 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: destroyed
trap: Fix: ask can a word make you angry, or hopeful? Student names one.
notes.prep: The one technical word today, linked to emotion so it sticks.

slides.title: Powerful, but true
lines: Plain: Melting ice is bad for polar bears.
Powerful and true: Melting ice leaves polar bears stranded and starving.
Too far: Melting ice is murdering every bear on Earth!

notes.answer: upgrade the plain word, then check: is it still true?
beats: POINT to Plain.
SAY: Bad. It's true, but it doesn't make me feel anything.
POINT to Powerful and true.
SAY: Stranded and starving. I can see it, and scientists say it happens.
That's the one I want.
POINT to Too far.
SAY: Murdering every bear? That isn't true. If I exaggerate, my reader stops trusting me.
ASK: Which word did I swap for bad?
5 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: stranded and starving
trap: picking the biggest word, even if it isn't true.
Fix: ask could a scientist say this? Student tones it to true.
notes.stretch: Make the plain sentence powerful a different way.
notes.help: Swap one word only, from the Power Word Bank.
notes.prep: The model. Critical feature: the word changes the feeling, but it must stay true. The near-miss (too far) is shown beside the target.

slides.title: Swap it
slides.pivot: picture it: what would you see or feel?
slides.followUp: cold call one board: is your word still true?

items.expect: starving. ACCEPT: any true, stronger word

items.say: Urgent. It means it can't wait. Tick or fix.

say: Write a powerful word to replace the plain one. Keep it true.
trap: swapping for a longer word that means the same, like large for big.
Fix: ask does it make you feel more? Student picks again.
notes.stretch: Give two swaps, one stronger than the other.
notes.help: Use the Plain to powerful table on the Power Word Bank.
notes.prep: Guided swapping, nouns and verbs both. SC2.

slides.title: Which sentence is powerful AND true?

options.text: Plastic is killing every single animal in the ocean!
options.misconception: exaggeration; strong but untrue, so readers stop trusting

options.text: Plastic bags choke sea turtles that mistake them for jellyfish.
Plastic is not very good for the ocean and its animals.
options.misconception: true but plain; the reader feels nothing

notes.answer: B - choke is powerful, and it really happens
beats: SAY: Three writers, same issue. Only one is powerful and true.
ASK: Which sentence is powerful AND true?
10 sec. Cue: voices off, everyone points to A, B or C.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: what's wrong with A?
Less -> test each: could a scientist say this?, re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: B. Choke makes us feel it, and turtles really do mistake bags for jellyfish.
trap: pointing to A because it is the most dramatic.
Fix: ask is every single animal dying? Student re-chooses.
notes.prep: Decision point. Under 80% means a second Plain / Powerful / Too far sort on the board before the word families.

slides.title: Build a word family
lines: The ending changes the job: a thing, or a describing word.

notes.answer: add a suffix to change the word's job; check the spelling change
beats: POINT to protect.
SAY: Protect is a doing word. Add ion: protection, a thing.
Add ive: protective, a describing word.
POINT to persuasion.
SAY: Careful. Persuade drops its d e and takes sion. Persuasion.
ASK: Persuade plus ive. Spell it.
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: persuasive
trap: Fix: student drops the e before ive, rereads.
notes.stretch: Find a fourth family member: protector, persuader.
notes.help: Build only the ion column first.
notes.prep: Spelling and morphology focus: suffixes change the job and sometimes the spelling (VC2E5LY04, LY05). SC3.

slides.title: Build it
slides.pivot: say the word slowly, clap the parts, then spell
slides.followUp: cold call one board: what changed in the spelling?

items.answer: destruction - the y and the end change
items.expect: destruction. ACCEPT: close tries, then fix
items.say: Destruction. Destroy changes more than most. Tick or fix.

say: Write it on your board, spelled right.
trap: Fix: student says it aloud, hears no e sound, drops it.
notes.stretch: Use each word in a persuasive phrase.
notes.help: Check the Word families table on the Power Word Bank.
notes.prep: Guided spelling. Destruction is the edge case. SC3.

slides.title: Upgrade challenge
slides.task: Work through your Worksheet. Finish by upgrading one of your Week 1 paragraphs with five powerful, true words.

notes.answer: five upgrades, each powerful and still true
beats: POINT to the task.
SAY: Pick your opening or your rebuttal from last week.
Rewrite it underneath with five upgrades.
SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Finished? Extension next. Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE. Ask: is that still true? Could a scientist say it?
ASK: How many upgrades so far?
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: 3 to 5
TIME 15 minutes. At 12, swap books and read your partner's best upgrade.
trap: upgrades that exaggerate: every, never, millions.
Fix: student checks each against the Too far column.
notes.stretch: Extension: the same event in two writers' words, then cheer-or-upset versions.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: choices with hints, a first swap done, a word family started.
notes.prep: Independent application on students' own Week 1 writing. SC2 and SC3.

slides.extendedTask: a worksheet ending in a Week 1 paragraph rewritten with five powerful, true words

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: The trees in the rainforest are getting cut down fast.
Upgrade it with one powerful word that is still true.

notes.answer: e.g. The rainforest is being destroyed / cleared / stripped at an alarming rate
beats: SAY: A new sentence about a new place. Upgrade it.
ASK: Rewrite the sentence with one powerful, true word.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: destroyed, cleared, stripped, vanishing
RECORD who goes too far, like every tree is gone. Tomorrow's warm-up.
trap: All the trees in the world are dead!
Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 on a new topic. One board per student.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Read your partner your best before-and-after upgrade. Which word did the most work?

notes.answer: open - listen for a verb or adjective that changed the feeling
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can lines together. Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can choose powerful, true words?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit boards.
ASK: Read your partner your best upgrade.
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: hungry became starving
notes.prep: Self-assessment read beside the exit boards. Students keep the Power Word Bank in their books for drafting. SC2.
